transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. We need to finalize the production message-streaming platform decision for the customer-notification service before the next integration milestone. The draft architecture recommends StreamGrid based on simpler operational setup and an initial capacity estimate of four brokers, and both finalists met our benchmark of 20,000 messages per second with sub-250-millisecond median delivery latency. Before I record a decision, I want to hear from each of you — backend, support engineering, security, and FinOps — on any concerns or sign-off issues with either KafkaCloud or StreamGrid. Let's start with backend.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go further. While testing the notification client's retry behavior this morning, I confirmed that the service already has a KafkaCloud-compatible producer and consumer path. That means using KafkaCloud would require only about two days of adapter cleanup, whereas moving to StreamGrid would require a new two-week client integration. I haven't updated the architecture document with this yet, but it directly affects the StreamGrid recommendation — the simpler operational setup comes with a significantly heavier client-side integration effort that isn't reflected in the current draft.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical requirement that I haven't added to the review ticket yet. During a customer escalation yesterday, I confirmed that three enterprise customers require notifications for each account to remain in order. KafkaCloud can guarantee that ordering using a customer_id partition key, but StreamGrid's tested mode cannot provide that ordering guarantee. This is a hard requirement from those enterprise customers and should be factored into the platform decision before we sign off.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a security concern that I confirmed during a data-flow review this afternoon. The notification payloads contain phone numbers, which means they fall under our data residency requirements and must be stored and processed in eu-central-1. KafkaCloud offers that processing region for this service, but StreamGrid's selected tier does not. I haven't filed the security architecture note yet, but this is a hard constraint — if StreamGrid's tier can't process in eu-central-1, it can't handle these payloads compliantly. This needs to be resolved before I can sign off on security.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share a FinOps finding from this morning's cloud account reconciliation. We already have existing KafkaCloud reserved-capacity credits that cover exactly six production brokers through the service's first year. StreamGrid has no equivalent credit. I should also note that I have not amended the four-broker estimate in the draft architecture document, so the current capacity estimate doesn't yet reflect this cost advantage on the KafkaCloud side.
transcript.speaker: A5
